answers.text: I'm an MBBS doctor and have worked for five years, the last three as a medical officer in a 120-bed private hospital in Ahmedabad. I cover outpatient and emergency shifts and make the monthly duty rota for eight junior doctors, though that is an informal duty. I was also part of a hospital committee that reduced the discharge delay from 4 hours to 2.5. That is when I realised how much patient experience depends on operations. I want an MBA to move into hospital management.
Healthcare is a noble field, and I believe in patient-centric care. I would like to leverage my clinical background and transform healthcare delivery with a holistic approach.
I can't give any case details or patient numbers beyond the general shift load. Patient information is protected, so I don't use even anonymised examples in interviews.
I don't agree that doctors are poor at management. We run emergencies, coordinate teams and decide under pressure. What we lack is financial training, and that is what I am asking the MBA for.
I was appointed as the hospital's operations head last year, and I manage the nursing staff and administration. That is my formal role.
